title: When "Neutral" Means Irrelevant: A Construct-Validity Audit of NormAd-ETI
abstract: arXiv:2611.32614v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: NormAd-ETI scores a model's judgment of everyday actions as acceptable, unacceptable, or neither as the cultural context shrinks from a specific rule to a country name. We audit what that three-way score measures. It combines two decisions: whether a supplied norm applies, and whether the action conforms to it. Separating them shows that when only a country is shown, applicability falls to near chance while conformity stays well above it, because the prompt withholds the rule a Neutral label depends on. Because one answer carries both decisions, the score follows the steadier conformity and hides the weaker applicability, and no single prompt recovers the two separately. Dedicated forced-choice probes separate them for frontier models but not for small open models, where the applicability judgment still tracks the hidden acceptability label. translated_title: 当“中性”意味着无关：对NormAd-ETI基准的结构效度审计
translated_abstract: NormAd-ETI基准在文化背景从具体规则缩减为国家名称时，评估模型对日常行为作出“可接受、不可接受或中性”判断的能力。本文审计了这一三方评分实际测量的是什么。该评分结合了两个决策：所提供的规范是否适用，以及行为是否符合该规范。将两者分离后显示，当提示词中只给出国家名称时，适用性判断降至接近随机水平，而符合性判断仍远高于随机水平，原因在于提示词省略了“中性”标签所依赖的规则。由于一个答案同时承载这两个决策，评分会跟随更稳定的符合性判断，而掩盖较弱的适用性判断，且没有任何单一提示词能将两者分别恢复出来。专门的强制选择题探针能够对前沿模型实现两个决策的分离，但对小型开源模型则无效——在这些模型上，适用性判断仍然追踪着隐藏的可接受性标签。添加书面理由说明可以减少这种混淆，但无法完全消除。我们建议报告……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文审计了NormAd-ETI基准的结构效度，发现其三方评分混淆了“规范是否适用”与“行为是否符合规范”这两个决策，导致在仅给出国家名称时适用性判断接近随机水平却被评分掩盖，并建议采用专门的强制选择题探针将两者分离。
en_tdlr: This construct-validity audit of NormAd-ETI reveals that its three-way score conflates norm applicability with action conformity—masking near-chance applicability when only a country is given—and recommends dedicated forced-choice probes to separate the two decisions.
